title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, as far as it can be inferred from this and the neighbouring pages. M is the arithmetic fundamental group of the moduli stack M_{1,1} over Q. It is an extension of Π_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q) by SL(2,Z)^ (the previous page writes 𝔖^{+∧} ≅ SL(2,Z)^). ρ is an elliptic element of order 3 or 6. It corresponds to the orbifold point j=0, the curve with complex multiplication by Z[ρ], whose automorphism group is μ_6. Inside M Grothendieck considers:
- N_ρ^*, a normalizer-type subgroup of ρ;
- Z_ρ, the centralizer of ρ;
- Z_ρ^! = M'(-j̄), a subgroup attached to the point (or tangential base point) written '-j̄', which maps isomorphically onto a subgroup of Π_Q^~;
- N_ρ^?, an intermediate group with N_ρ^? of index 3 in N_ρ^*.
The page records the following, in order.
(i) The chain N_ρ^? ⊂_3 N_ρ^* ⊂ M, with M'(-j̄) of index 4 in N_ρ^?. These are the subgroups that contain the partial sections M(-j̄) ≅ Π_Q^~.
(ii) (32) defines M°(-j̄) := Ker(ε_2 : M'(-j̄) → μ), of index 2. It is rewritten as an intersection with Z_ρ and then with N_ρ^*. It is therefore a partial section over the group in (33).
(iii) (33) Π°_Q^~ := Ker((ε_2, ε_3) : Π_Q^~ → μ×μ). This is identified with the kernel of Π_Q^~ → Ẑ* → (Z/12)^*. Since (Z/12)^* = (Z/4)^* × (Z/3)^* ≅ μ×μ, ε_2 and ε_3 are the quadratic characters of Q(i) and Q(√-3). Π°_Q^~ is then essentially the absolute Galois group of Q(μ_12) = Q(i, √-3), the field over which the CM curve and its automorphisms of order 4 and 6 become rational.
(iv) Assuming, subject to a correction promised later, that an involution τ' normalizes M°(-j̄), (34) sets M'''(-j̄) := μ_{τ'} · M°(-j̄), a semidirect product with μ_{τ'} = {1, τ'}. This is a subgroup of index 4 in N_ρ^?.
(v) (35) M'''(-j̄) maps isomorphically to an intermediate index-2 extension Π'''_Q^~ of Π°_Q^~. So it is a partial section over a larger Galois group. The next page draws from this the decompositions N_ρ^* ≅ M'''·L_ρ and a dihedral description D_ρ = μ_12·L_ρ.
Overall purpose: describe the Galois sections (and partial sections over finite extensions of Q) of the M_{1,1} tower attached to the orbifold point j=0. The question is how far the decomposition group of that stacky point can be lifted, and how it sits inside the normalizer of the elliptic element. This continues the previous page's discussion of lifting Π_Q → 𝔖_3 to 𝔖̃_3 and of splittings of the extension M.
errors: The page itself flags that 'τ' normalise M°(-j̄)' holds only 'modulo une rectification'. The semidirect-product definition (34) is therefore provisional.

Index bookkeeping: the page says M''' has index 4 in 'N_ρ*'. The next page's diagram (37) gives M'''(-j) ⊂_4 N_ρ^?, consistent with [N^?:M'] = 4 and [M':M°] = 2. Read literally against N_ρ^* the index would be 12, so it should read N_ρ^?.
The intermediate rewriting in (32) (Z_ρ ∩ M'''^!, then N_ρ^* ∩ M°^!) is partly struck through and only half-legible. Its exact form cannot be verified.

ideas.what: Decomposition and partial-section subgroups attached to the elliptic (orbifold) point j=0 inside the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1}, and their position in the normalizer and centralizer of an elliptic element ρ of SL(2,Z)^
ideas.modern_name: Galois sections at stacky/orbifold points; normalizers of torsion in profinite SL2 and in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller setting
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps (1990s); later anabelian work on orbifold sections
ideas.where_published: Only hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme (M_{1,1}, SL(2,Z)^ and the Galois action)

ideas.what: Identifying Ker(ε_2, ε_3) with Ker(Π → (Z/12)^*), i.e. with Gal over Q(μ_12) = Q(i, √-3), the field of definition of the extra automorphisms at j=0 and j=1728
ideas.modern_name: Cyclotomic character mod 12; field of definition of CM automorphisms

ideas.what: Enlarging a partial section by a semidirect factor generated by an involution τ' normalizing it
ideas.modern_name: Extension of Galois sections over quadratic extensions

missed.claim: A detailed lattice of subgroups (indices 2, 3, 4, 6, 12) describing exactly over which subfields of Q(μ_12) the decomposition group of the orbifold point j=0 of M_{1,1} gives genuine sections. It is accompanied by a dihedral description of the normalizer N_ρ^* ≅ μ_12·L_ρ on the next page. The 'rectification' about τ' is left pending.
missed.quote: Modulo une rectification que je vais faire plus bas, τ' normalise M°(-j̄)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a fine-grained account of sections at stacky points of M_{1,1} and of how they relate to GT-type normalizer computations. It is close in spirit to later work on Galois action at elliptic points, but this explicit index bookkeeping is not, to my knowledge, published in this form. Interest is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful, mostly routine bookkeeping of subgroups and indices in a setting (Galois action on SL(2,Z)^ and the elliptic points of M_{1,1}) that was later developed by Ihara, Nakamura and others. It is an unpublished detail, but not a striking new idea.
transcription_corrections: 'sous-groupe d'indice 4 de N_{ρ*}' should read N_ρ^? (the superscript is a question mark), consistent with diagram (37).
The first line reads 'Revenons aux sous-groupes [struck N_ρ^?] des', followed by the displayed chain.
In (32) the final '!' marks attached to M''' and M° are decorations of the handwriting; the struck-through portion is illegible.
